applicability: All patients after instruction.
adequacy: Adequate when a program is taught (usually during PT) and ongoing independent adherence is documented.

applicability: Analgesia as risk profile allows.
adequacy: Scheduled trial of about 2-4 weeks at therapeutic dose, or documented intolerance/contraindication; lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

applicability: Persistent neuropathic intercostal/radicular pain after surgery.
adequacy: Titrate to effective/tolerated dose (e.g., gabapentin 1200-1800 mg/day or pregabalin 150-300 mg/day) for about 4-8 weeks; optional - absence does not preclude MMI.

applicability: Chronic post-surgical pain with psychosocial contributors; part of SCS screening.
adequacy: Initial 3-4 sessions over 2 weeks; up to about 6-10 sessions over 5-6 weeks with documented functional improvement.

applicability: Refractory neuropathic pain 6 months or more despite conventional management, after successful trial.
adequacy: Requires psychological screening and a successful trial (50% or more relief); adequate once implanted and programming optimized; not required for MMI if not a candidate or declined.

applicability: Chronic disabling post-surgical pain with no surgical target.
adequacy: Continuation beyond 2 weeks requires documented objective gains; total generally 20 full-day sessions (or part-day equivalent) or fewer.

applicability: Identified target only: nonunion, hardware failure or junctional disease concordant with symptoms.

applicability: Adjunct for established or high-risk nonunion.
adequacy: Worn per prescribed daily protocol until radiographic fusion or about 9 months; optional adjunct - absence does not preclude MMI.

applicability: Symptom-limited; avoid aggressive loading.
adequacy: Post-op benchmarks roughly 16 visits/8 weeks after decompression and up to about 34 visits/16 weeks after fusion (lumbar ODG-style, extrapolated); continue only with objective gains.

applicability: Symptomatic CT-confirmed nonunion or hardware failure.

applicability: Deep wound or implant infection: source control first.
adequacy: Adequate once source control achieved (one or more debridements); implant retention for early infection with stable hardware, exchange/removal for chronic infection or loosening.

adequacy: Culture-directed course, typically at least 12 weeks after debridement for implant infection (IV start, oral step-down acceptable); adequate when course completed with clinical/lab (CRP/ESR) resolution, or long-term suppression is established.

applicability: Chronic infection or failed/loose hardware: implant removal or exchange.
